# ERC REPORT - SIH26113 Maternity Assist Belt

## How this was produced

`scripts/validate_erc.py` runs eleven rule groups against the same design model that generates the `.sch`, so every finding below is genuinely present in the schematic. It is **not** Autodesk EAGLE's own ERC.

> **NOT EXECUTED - TOOL UNAVAILABLE:** EAGLE / Fusion Electronics is not installed in the environment where these files were produced, so *EAGLE's* ERC has not been run. Running it is step 6 of PCB_BUILD_GUIDE.md. The independent check below is what can be claimed today.

## Rules checked

| # | Rule |
|---|---|
| R1 | reference designators unique; every deviceset exists in the library |
| R2 | every (part, pin) in the netlist names a pin that exists |
| R3 | every pin of every part is on exactly one net - no floating pins, no pin on two nets |
| R4 | no net has fewer than two connections, except declared no-connects |
| R5 | every net feeding a power pin also carries a supply symbol |
| R6 | no net has two or more push-pull outputs |
| R7 | no net has inputs but no driver |
| R8 | each I2C line has exactly one pull-up; no address clash on a bus |
| R9 | ESP32-S3: analog only on ADC1; strapping pins flagged; every module pin in the GPIO table |
| R10 | MOSFET gates have a pull-down; inductive loads have a correctly-oriented flyback diode; clamp polarity |
| R11 | every LED has a series resistor |

## Intentional exceptions

| Item | Why it is acceptable |
|---|---|
| `LDO_NC` is a single-pin net | AP2112 pin 4 is documented as "No Connection" (Diodes DS39724 Rev.2-2). Leaving it unconnected is the datasheet's own instruction. Declared explicitly in `validate_erc.py` rather than silenced. |
| `IMU_OCS_AUX` goes only to test point TP7 | The LSM6DSOX datasheet (DS12814 Rev.4, Table 1 note 2) says to leave OCS_Aux *electrically* unconnected but soldered to the board. An isolated land satisfies both halves of that instruction, and it is not a floating input on a net with a driver. |
| `TMP_ALERT` goes to a pull-up and a test point, not to a GPIO | The pin budget has no spare GPIO. TMP117 alerts are readable over I2C by polling the configuration register, so the hardware ALERT line is a convenience, not a requirement. |
| `AS_OUT`, `AS_PGO`, `HX_BASE`, `HX_XO` go to test points | All four are datasheet-designated "NC when not used" or optional-function pins. Bringing them to a land keeps them probeable without committing a GPIO. |
| `0x36` appears on both I2C busses | This is the resolution of a real conflict, not an oversight - see DESIGN_ASSUMPTIONS.md. The AS5600 and the MAX17048 both have a fixed 0x36 address and are therefore put on physically separate busses. |
